title: Intelligent recap: what Teams generates after a meeting or call, and what controls it
summary: The licensing, storage, policy paths and commands are supported by Microsoft documentation, and the page discloses the conflicting guidance about whether the recap switches take effect. Minor corrections should acknowledge two further documentation discrepancies and remove a checklist item whose licensing control has no table row.

claims.claim: Intelligent recap supplies AI-generated meeting notes after meetings and events.
claims.quote:
After the meeting or event ends, your users can access the following AI powered features for their meetings through the Recap tab in the Teams calendar and chat:
- AI meeting notes

claims.claim: Intelligent recap includes AI-recommended tasks.
claims.quote: AI recommended tasks

claims.quote:

- Speaker timeline markers show who spoke during the meeting, when they spoke, and allows your users to jump to that moment.

claims.quote: Meeting chapters divide the meeting into chapters, and meeting topics that allow your users to jump to a point in the meeting when a certain topic was discussed.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Why it matters; Risks and limits; Governance controls; What to check
claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policyname> -AllowIntelligentRecap $false disables recap for all meetings under the policy, according to the no-transcript page.
claims.quote:
Turning off intelligent recap disables intelligent recap for all meetings, regardless of whether transcripts are saved.

To turn off intelligent recap, use the Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy cmdlet and set the -AllowIntelligentRecap parameter to $false.

claims.claim: The related Teams settings become unavailable when intelligent recap is disabled.
claims.quote: Turning off intelligent recap disables intelligent recap for all meetings, regardless of whether transcripts are saved, and the related settings are unavailable in Teams.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscription $true allows meeting transcription.
claims.quote: Determines whether post-meeting captions and transcriptions are allowed in a user's meetings. Set this to TRUE to allow. Set this to FALSE to prohibit.

claims.quote:
In the Microsoft Teams admin center, select Voice > Calling policies.
2. Select the policy you want to modify.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTranscriptionForCalling $true enables call transcription.
claims.quote:
For example, this script enables transcription for the global policy:

```powershell
Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity Global -AllowTranscriptionForCalling $true
```

claims.claim: Call transcription is off by default.
claims.quote: When turned on, the transcript is available to users to review after a call ends. This setting is off by default.

claims.claim: The Copilot policy setting is in Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Recording & transcription > Copilot.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting policies.
2. Select an existing policy or create a new one.
3. Go to the Recording & transcription section and find the Copilot setting.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -Copilot Disabled sets the organizer's default Copilot option to Off.
claims.quote:
To set the organizer's default Copilot option to Off and allow them to change it, use the following script:

```PowerShell
Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -Copilot Disabled
```

The differing reference is https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamsmeetingpolicy.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -NewMeetingRecordingExpirationDays <days> sets recording and transcript expiration.
claims.quote:
To set the expiration time using PowerShell, run the following command:

```powershell

```

claims.claim: Meeting policies can be assigned to groups or individual users.
claims.quote: You can apply your Copilot meeting policies to groups or individual users.

claims.claim: There is no separate policy setting for no-transcript recap; disabling it while keeping Copilot enabled uses the general intelligent recap policy switch.
claims.quote: There isn't a separate policy setting for intelligent recap without saving transcripts. To prevent users from using this feature while keeping Copilot enabled, turn off intelligent recap in the Teams meeting policy.

claims.claim: Meeting organizers can delete a no-transcript AI summary from the Recap tab.
claims.quote: Meeting organizers can delete the AI summary from the Recap tab or the corresponding Word document in OneDrive.

claims.claim: No admin switch for organizer deletion of no-transcript AI summaries is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams intelligent recap AI summary delete administrator control policy; "intelligent recap" "delete" "admin" "summary". Read no-transcript recap FAQ and meeting memory deletion guidance. Neither documents an admin switch controlling organizer deletion of the Word summary.

claims.claim: Organizers can change the Copilot meeting option when the assigned policy value permits overrides.
claims.quote: Organizers can change this value to Only during the meeting, and Off.

claims.claim: The AllowIntelligentRecap guidance specifies meetings but does not state whether the parameter also disables call recap.
claims.quote: Searched: AllowIntelligentRecap Teams calls intelligent recap calling policy. Read no-transcript recap, call recap prerequisites, Teams Premium call recap and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy. AllowIntelligentRecap is described for meetings, with no stated call applicability.

claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet "Confirm which users hold Teams Premium or Copilot licences, and Teams Phone for PSTN calls." The licence requirements remain in Cost and licensing; no new controls row is requested.
